prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its active form that enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-achievement B021 prize to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange showed that all six of us rest the case on the science and not on the shared first place, and I agree with that. The chain from human incretin physiology (Holst), through proglucagon processing, receptor biology and GLP-1/GLP-2 biology (Drucker), to identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) amide (Mojsov), is a discovery arc in which each named person owns a distinct step. It was independently replicated for about three decades and has produced drugs with documented glycaemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal outcome effects. It is mature, the mechanism is not in dispute, and I see no other shortlisted candidate that combines this much basic physiology with this size of medical consequence. The citation should name the physiology and the active form and describe treatment only as something the discoveries enabled.
statement.case_against: The attribution remains the weak point, and the chair is right that agreement on rank does not settle it. Mojsov's share rests on a priority question involving Habener, who is not among the supplied credited names, and the supplied record does not let me resolve it. Knudsen's development of long-acting analogues is a distinct contribution that the three-person limit forces us to leave out, and a citation that mentions treatment can be read as slighting her. A two-part prize is not feasible here, because B021 alone has four credited names and any second part would exceed three people. If the committee cannot sustain Mojsov on the documented record, the fallback I would take is Holst and Drucker only on B021, or B022 as a clean two-person prize, and not a hurried substitution.

responses.point: The Mojsov dispute is about priority and not about whether her identification and synthesis of the active peptide was essential, so the citation can describe that contribution without adjudicating who was first; leaving Habener off still means choosing a side.
responses.response: I move toward your position. In round 1 I treated the Habener question as open and left the citation wording fairly loose. I now think your point is the practical way through: the citation should state GLP-1 physiology and its active form and make no claim about who first found the peptide. I would add that this only helps if the committee can say what Mojsov's contribution was in the documented record, which is synthesis and demonstration of the active amide as insulinotropic. We also read B012 differently. You hold it back because Cerami, Vilcek and Kollias are uncredited. I make the same attribution objection to B012, but I still carry it as a fallback because its maturity is complete, and that is why it replaces B052 among my alternatives.

responses.point: Dropping Knudsen should be stated openly as a choice about the type of contribution and not a judgment of her importance; if Mojsov cannot be defended, he would rewrite the B021 citation around Holst and Drucker instead of abandoning the candidate.
responses.response: I agree with the framing, and my co-authorship with you is not a reason to avoid saying so. The committee should record that excluding Knudsen is a discovery-versus-development decision. I also accept your fallback as the right order of operations: if the Mojsov credit fails, a Holst and Drucker prize on B021 keeps the strongest candidate on the table and is better than moving to a weaker one. Where I still differ is that the two-person version is less complete, since it loses the identification of the active peptide, so I would only take it if the evidence actually fails and not because the dispute is merely uncomfortable.

responses.point: The chair's questions ask whether Mojsov can be sustained against Habener, whether Knudsen is left out on a discovery-versus-development basis, and whether the citation should mention treatment.
responses.response: On your questions: I would sustain Mojsov for the identification and synthesis of the active peptide, while saying openly that the supplied record cannot settle priority and that my recollection is not a source. I accept leaving out Knudsen on the discovery basis, with the same caveat. On the citation, I keep a treatment clause but word it as the discoveries having enabled incretin-based therapies, so that it does not imply credit to the drug developers. I also note that your fallback, a Holst and Drucker pair, is the same one I would use, and I would apply it only if the committee decides the identification question cannot be defended.

responses.point: Excluding Knudsen will be read by some as undervaluing the step that produced the therapies, a citation that mentions treatment risks implying credit to the drug developers, and he asked that decisive-contribution claims be tested against the primary record and not recall.
responses.response: I agree on all three points, and I would keep the test you propose. The weakness of our whole discussion is that every member, myself included, states these histories from memory, and the chair's summary says so. You also commented on my CAR-T ranking in round 1. I accept your objection that the field is still evolving and the chimeric receptor origin lies partly with Eshhar, and that is why I no longer carry B052 as an alternative. I now think B022 is the better first fallback: the mechanism is conceptually complete and the Mori and Walter attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's credit for the active GLP-1 peptide can be defended against Habener's priority claim; the supplied record does not resolve it and my recollection is not a source.
Whether the committee will accept leaving out Knudsen, or whether weighting drug development more heavily would displace a basic discoverer.
Whether a citation mentioning treatment can be worded so that it does not imply credit to the drug developers who are not laureates.
My recollection of the GLP-1, CAR-T and TNF-blockade histories has not been checked against primary sources.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have co-authored work with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisén and share an institution (Karolinska Institutet) with several colleagues. Neither involves a shortlisted candidate or any credited name on B021, B022 or B012, and shared affiliation alone is not treated as a conflict. No recusal is indicated.
